uses_raw_diagonal.context: This script does not call np.diag itself -- it delegates mass computation to diagnostic_blocks.domain_community_volumes(cross_domain_handling=...). So despite the script's name '_corrected_check', the 'correction' it tests is only the anchor/cross-domain crediting formula (naive vs excluded vs split), NOT a Hungarian/permutation correction of the diagonal reading. This is explicit and intentional per both docstrings, not a hidden bug, but the naming invites misreading -- worth flagging for adjudication.

purpose_one_line: Single-seed pilot sweep of the in-loop domain-balance penalty (make_inloop_domain_balance_penalty_torch) across weights {0,1,5,20,50} on C3/K4 and C6/K4, checking (1) whether r_k moves toward 0.5 as weight increases, (2) gauge-safety via u_scales_cv, and (3) whether an independent Z_scaled-based outer-loop reading (mass_tvd) tracks the real U_prob-based improvement.

notable_facts: This is the earliest/single-seed pilot in the inloop_* family; its own docstring says its C3/K4 result was noisy/non-monotonic, which directly motivated domain_balance_inloop_seedcheck.py's paired-seed follow-up -- a clear provenance chain worth preserving in the audit narrative.

Docstring explicitly frames point 3 as 'THE POINT 8 QUESTION' (ticket 82 point 8) and states the expectation from the algebraic proof is 'no visible effect' on u_scales_cv if the penalty is truly gauge-safe -- CLAUDE.md's E2 section reports this in-loop mechanism was built on U_prob specifically because a Z_scaled-based candidate (elsewhere, make_domain_balance_penalty_torch, not this script) was found exploitable. This script is testing the gauge-safety of the U_prob-based penalty, not the exploitable Z_scaled one -- worth not conflating the two in adjudication.

purpose_one_line: Before building any ticket-82 binding_penalty mechanism, checks whether per-community social/semantic balance is already roughly even on production fits using the Z_scaled mass basis with NO Hungarian/permutation correction applied (raw diagonal), matching what a Module-2 differentiable in-loop term would actually see -- across C1-C6 x K in {2,4}, two normalization variants (v8-style absolute, within-domain share).
local_reimplementations: domain_balance_for_cell: computes soc_vol/sem_vol by directly summing np.abs(np.diag(Z_final[r])) over active relations, rather than calling diagnostic_blocks.domain_community_volumes (which did not yet exist at this script's original write time, per the later domain_balance_corrected_check.py's docstring calling this script's formula 'the naive formula'/'the first ... test'). This is the SOURCE of the naive/raw baseline that domain_balance_corrected_check.py later re-tests via domain_community_volumes's 'naive' treatment -- so it is a duplication in the sense that domain_community_volumes(cross_domain_handling='naive') now reproduces this script's formula inside diagnostic_blocks, but that consolidation happened AFTER this script, and this script's own docstring is explicit that its formula is 'provisional... NOT the final ticket-82 design.' Not a silent drift; an acknowledged historical precursor.

uses_raw_diagonal.context: np.abs(np.diag(Z_final[r])) for both soc_vol and sem_vol accumulation (lines 52 and 55). This IS the raw, uncorrected reading -- but it is explicitly and deliberately so: the module docstring states 'with NO permutation correction applied (raw diagonal, matching what a Module-2 differentiable term would actually see)' and frames the raw choice as the deliberate point of the test (a would-be in-loop penalty could only ever see the raw diagonal, since Hungarian assignment is a discontinuous op restricted to the outer loop per CLAUDE.md §4.1). This is an intentional raw baseline, clearly labeled as such in-file, not a bug or an oversight -- it is NOT compared against a corrected reading within this same file (no Hungarian-corrected variant computed here), only against a different *normalization* of the same raw quantity (formula (a) vs (b)). The corrected-vs-raw comparison happens in a later, separate script/mechanism (facet_relation_profile / domain_community_volumes), not inside this file.

notable_facts: Docstring explicitly says results 'match FINDINGS §15/16/17's grid' (C1-C6 x K in {2,4}, production settings) -- a specific cross-reference Stage B/adjudication could verify against FINDINGS.md.

Explicitly does NOT resolve which normalization ((a) v8-style absolute vs (b) within-domain-share) is 'the' right one -- states both variants inherit the anchor double-counting concern equally so the naive-vs-corrected comparison (handled by the later domain_balance_corrected_check.py) isn't confounded by normalization choice. A deliberately scoped, single-variable test.

This is chronologically the earliest of the two anchor-handling scripts (domain_balance_corrected_check.py is the explicit follow-up), and the 'no correction' in its filename refers to the Hungarian-permutation dimension, not the anchor-crediting dimension that domain_balance_corrected_check.py addresses -- two different scripts are each 'correcting' a different, independent axis of the same underlying formula, which is worth being precise about in any downstream write-up that cites both by name.
